the_stream_diff_that_explains_it.finding: INSTRUMENT DEFECT, located precisely: agents' materializers progressed through params fix, watermark read and UDS routing (streams show vex-q-watermark + uds-q-events — none of which before had) and then died with KeyError reading the stub's rows. The stub ignores each query's SELECT column list and serves a fixed row shape copied from the REFERENCE'S aliases; the inspected solution wrote `e.id AS uds_event_id` (a different-but-valid alias) and read ev['uds_event_id'] -> KeyError. It also chose its own watermark-table schema — legitimate, since the era's DDL is not in the workspace — which the stub cannot know.

Reference and altformat share those choices, so the admission trio (before/after/alt) was structurally unable to catch it.

lessons_mechanical: a recording stub's row shape is part of the instrument: it must PROJECT canonical rows onto each query's requested aliases, never serve reference-shaped rows

schema invented by the fix (the watermark table) must be either discoverable in the workspace (SCHEMA.md/DDL) or the stub must accept any schema choice — otherwise the fixture grades an invisible convention

the valid-variant pool must include an ALIAS-VARYING variant: the altformat varied a write pattern but shared every alias with the reference, so alias-pinning predicates and surfaces survived the filter
